extracted.intended_audience: Employers, safety and health professionals, labor representatives, state-plan agencies, small business representatives, and other stakeholders who must implement or comment on the proposed OSHA heat standard (NPRM Docket No. OSHA-2021-0009).
extracted.subtask_description: Extract and apply the criteria and requirements in OSHA's Notice of Proposed Rulemaking for 'Heat Injury and Illness Prevention in Outdoor and Indoor Work Settings' (NPRM) to evaluate employer obligations and the proposed regulatory elements. Useful for commenters, compliance planners, and regulators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph (a) Scope and Application
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard would apply to all employers conducting outdoor and indoor work in all general industry, construction, maritime, and agriculture sectors where OSHA has jurisdiction, with some exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines industries, work activities, and explicit exemptions (e.g., certain short-duration exposures, telework, cooled vehicles, indoor areas maintained below specified temperatures). OSHA requests comments on scope and applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph (b) Definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions for terms used in the standard (e.g., initial heat trigger, high heat trigger, acclimatization, heat index, WBGT, heat illness, excessively high heat area, rest break, break area, employer-provided cooling, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the operative meanings that determine when and how requirements apply; OSHA solicits comment on proposed definitions and alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph (c) Heat Injury and Illness Prevention Plan (HIIPP)
rubrics_metrics.description: A programmatic requirement that employers create, implement, and maintain a written heat injury and illness prevention plan to evaluate and control heat hazards in their workplace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies plan elements (identifying hazards, response, acclimatization, training, recordkeeping, etc.), frequency of review, and accessibility. OSHA requests comment on required content and whether model plans should be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph (d) Identifying Heat Hazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Employer obligation to identify workplace heat hazards, including evaluating environmental and job-related heat sources and exposures (ambient conditions, heat-generating processes, PPE, metabolic heat from work).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May require environmental monitoring or other methods; employers must document hazard identification in the HIIPP. OSHA requests comment on methods and thresholds for identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph (e) Requirements at or Above the Initial Heat Trigger
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of protective measures that become required when environmental conditions meet or exceed the 'initial heat trigger'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes timing, drinking water, break areas, indoor controls, fan evaluation, acclimatization, rest breaks if needed, effective communication, and PPE. OSHA requests comment on the trigger metric and required measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial Heat Trigger (basis and use)
rubrics_metrics.description: A temperature/heat-exposure threshold (based on Heat Index, WBGT, or Ambient Temperature) that triggers the initial set of employer requirements under paragraph (e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA explains observational and experimental evidence supporting the trigger, compares state standards and NGO recommendations, and requests comments on the trigger values and measurement method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing (actions tied to triggers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements specifying when measures must be implemented relative to initial and high heat triggers (e.g., start of shift, during time-at-or-above-trigger).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on how employers should time protective measures; OSHA solicits comments about practicability and timing details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drinking Water
rubrics_metrics.description: Employers must provide an adequate supply of potable drinking water at no cost when at or above the initial heat trigger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA discusses placement, accessibility, quantity guidance, and requests comments on details of water provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Break Area(s) at Outdoor Work Sites
rubrics_metrics.description: Employers must provide accessible shaded or cooled break areas for outdoor workers when at or above the initial heat trigger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses type of shade/cooling (natural/shaded structures, vehicles with A/C), distance from work areas, and whether vehicles can serve as break areas; OSHA requests comments on standards for outdoor break areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Break Area(s) at Indoor Work Sites
rubrics_metrics.description: Employers must provide accessible cooled or otherwise appropriate break areas for indoor workers when at or above the initial heat trigger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses expectations where indoor cooling exists vs. where it does not, and requests comments on when separate break areas are necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indoor Work Area Controls (engineering controls)
rubrics_metrics.description: Engineering and administrative controls to reduce heat exposure in indoor workplaces (e.g., air-conditioning, humidity control, fans, evaporative coolers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA presents preliminary feasibility findings for indoor engineering controls and asks for comment on practicability and effectiveness of specific controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of Fan Use
rubrics_metrics.description: Employers must evaluate whether fan use is protective or harmful under specific environmental conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA notes that under some conditions fans may increase heat strain and provides guidance on evaluation; requests comments and evidence on fan effectiveness and risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acclimatization
rubrics_metrics.description: Employers must implement acclimatization measures to protect new or returning workers (gradual increase in exposure over days) when at or above the initial heat trigger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA summarizes evidence (tenure as a risk factor), recommends procedures for gradual exposure, and requests comment on specific acclimatization schedules and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rest Breaks if Needed (at or above initial trigger)
rubrics_metrics.description: Employers must provide rest breaks as needed based on hazard identification, workload, and worker condition once the initial trigger is met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA reviews evidence on rest breaks and provides options; requests comment on frequency/duration of breaks and alternatives (e.g., 15-minute/hour at high trigger in regulatory options).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective Communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Employers must ensure effective communication of heat hazards, triggers, controls, and emergency procedures to employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes language access, daily notifications tied to triggers, signage, and training linkage; OSHA requests comment on communication methods and required frequencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Employers must identify and provide appropriate PPE (including considerations where PPE increases heat burden) and integrate PPE decisions into hazard controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA discusses PPE tradeoffs with heat exposure and requests comment on PPE lists, use guidance, and mitigation when PPE increases heat stress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph (f) Requirements at or Above the High Heat Trigger
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of additional, more protective measures that become required when conditions meet or exceed the 'high heat trigger'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes timing, mandatory rest breaks, observation for signs/symptoms, hazard alerts, and designation/controls for excessively high heat areas. OSHA requests comments on high trigger values and measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: High Heat Trigger (basis and use)
rubrics_metrics.description: A higher temperature/heat-exposure threshold (based on Heat Index, WBGT, or Ambient Temperature) that triggers enhanced protections under paragraph (f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA explains observational and experimental evidence for choosing the high trigger, compares alternatives, and requests comment on numeric values and measurement approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rest Breaks (requirements at or above high trigger)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific rest break mandates when the high heat trigger is reached (background on provision, how to comply, frequency/duration expectations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA discusses a background rationale, gives compliance options, and seeks comment on required rest-break schedules and alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observation for Signs and Symptoms
rubrics_metrics.description: Employers must establish observation procedures for recognizing heat illness signs and symptoms and ensure timely response when at or above the high heat trigger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May include buddy systems, designated observers, procedures for responding to symptoms; OSHA requests comment on the specifics of observation practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hazard Alert
rubrics_metrics.description: Employers must issue hazard alerts to notify employees when the high heat trigger is met and when enhanced protections apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on content, method, and timing of alerts; OSHA requests comment on alert formats and requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excessively High Heat Areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification and additional controls (including signage/warning) for work areas where heat exposure is excessively high.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA describes what constitutes an excessively high heat area, recommended controls, and requests comment on thresholds and control measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph (g) Heat Illness and Emergency Response and Planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Employer requirements to prepare for and respond to heat illnesses, including emergency response planning, first-aid, evacuation, and medical treatment procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies planning elements, coordination with emergency services, access to medical care, and training links; OSHA requests comment on required plan content and response standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph (h) Training
rubrics_metrics.description: Required employee and supervisor training on heat hazards, recognition of heat illness, prevention measures, acclimatization, use of controls, and emergency procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA outlines training frequency, content expectations, language/accessibility considerations, and requests comment on training intervals and materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph (i) Recordkeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for employers to keep records related to heat hazard identification, HIIPP implementation, training, monitoring, incidents, and other compliance elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies types of records, retention periods, and availability to employees/OSHA; OSHA requests comment on burden and recordkeeping forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph (j) Requirements Implemented at No Cost to Employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision that employers must implement required protections without cost to employees (e.g., provide water, PPE, medical treatment, access to breaks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies which measures are employer responsibilities and requests comment on implementation and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph (k) Dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Specification of compliance dates, phased implementation timelines, and effective dates for different provisions of the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA provides proposed dates and requests comment on adequate lead time for employers, especially small entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph (l) Severability
rubrics_metrics.description: A severability clause describing that if any provision is invalidated, the remainder of the standard remains in force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard drafting provision; no technical guidance but included in NPRM text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk Assessment (reported incidence, fatalities, underreporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA's assessment of reported annual incidence of nonfatal heat-related injuries and illnesses, reported occupational heat-related fatalities, limitations, and undercounting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes data sources (BLS, workers' comp, ED visits), discussion of underreporting and methodology; OSHA solicits comments on data and underreporting adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for Initial and High Heat Triggers (evidence base)
rubrics_metrics.description: The scientific and regulatory basis (observational studies, experimental evidence, state standards, NGO recommendations) OSHA uses to set initial and high heat triggers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA summarizes supporting literature and seeks comment and alternative evidence or suggestions for triggers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk Reduction — Effectiveness of Control Measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of evidence on the effectiveness of individual control measures (rest breaks, shade, fans, water, acclimatization) and multicomponent interventions to reduce heat-related risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA summarizes systematic reviews, experimental and observational studies, and governmental/non-governmental guidance; requests comment on effectiveness and best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technological Feasibility (environmental monitoring and engineering controls)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of monitoring methods (Heat Index, WBGT, Ambient Temperature) and engineering controls (air-conditioning, humidity control, shade, evaporative coolers) for feasibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA presents preliminary feasibility findings for monitoring and controls in indoor, outdoor, mobile, and heat-generating-process workplaces; requests comments on feasibility and costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic Feasibility and Cost Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA's tests and analysis of the economic feasibility of the proposed standard, including screening tests, cost assumptions, affected entity profiling, unit costs of compliance, and total cost estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes treatment of small/very small entities, alternatives, sensitivity analyses, and SBAR panel input; OSHA requests comment on cost assumptions, estimates, and regulatory options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial Regulatory Flexibility Analysis & SBREFA Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of impacts on small entities, reporting/recordkeeping burdens, regulatory alternatives, and options to reduce small entity impacts as required under SBREFA/IRFA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA provides alternatives (e.g., thresholds, HIIPP exemptions for small employers, rest-break variants) and solicits comment on impacts and alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governmental and Non-Governmental Requirements and Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Review and comparison of existing state standards and non-governmental recommendations (e.g., CA, OR, WA, NIOSH guidance) that inform the proposed requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as supporting material for feasibility and effectiveness; OSHA requests comment on harmonization and differences with state/NGA standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental Monitoring Methods (Heat Index, WBGT, Ambient Temperature)
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptable environmental metrics and methodologies for assessing workplace heat (Heat Index, WBGT, Ambient Temperature) and guidance on their calculation and use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA provides methodological details, footnotes with formulas/sources, and asks for comments on preferred indices, measurement protocols, and instrument placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for States With OSHA-Approved State Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions and considerations for how the proposed standard would apply to states with OSHA-approved plans and any state-plan-specific requirements or timelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes federalism considerations and coordination; OSHA requests comment from state-plan authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heat Exposure Methodology Used in Distributional and Benefits Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods for calculating worker heat exposure for distributional and benefits/costs analysis (data merging, exposure calculations, demographic breakdowns).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical appendices describe data processing and assumptions; OSHA requests comment on methodology and data sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternatives and Regulatory Options
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed regulatory options and alternatives (e.g., requiring HIIPPs for all establishments, specific rest-break timing at high trigger, upper-bound exemptions for sedentary work, medical surveillance options).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA lists alternatives evaluated and asks for comments on their relative merits, burdens, and practicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heat-Related Training Content Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific recommended/required content for training programs (recognizing heat illness, emergency response, proper hydration, acclimatization, use of controls, employer duties).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA outlines minimum content elements, target audiences (supervisors vs. employees), frequency, and documentation; requests comment on necessary content and training intervals.
